title: The spend and precedence matrices that addMConstr takes

blocks.text: A water utility models its projects with gurobipy's matrix API (`addMVar`, `addMConstr`). Its projects are given as a list of `(project_id, start_year, cost_profile)` triples: a project that starts in year $`s`$ spends `cost_profile[k]` in year $`s + k`$. Write two functions that build the arrays its rows need, with one column per project, in the order of the list.
**`spend_matrix(projects, years)`** returns a NumPy array $`A`$ of shape `(len(years), len(projects))` with

and 0 elsewhere. Spend that falls in a year not in `years` (after the horizon) is left out: it is not this plan's money. Then `addMConstr(A, x, "<", B)` is the yearly budget row $`\sum_j A_{r,j}\, x_j \le B_r`$.

**`needs_matrix(projects, parent_of)`** returns one row per entry of the dict `parent_of` (child id to parent id), in the dict's order, with $`+1`$ in the child's column and $`-1`$ in the parent's: then `addMConstr(N, x, "<", 0)` states $`x_c - x_{p(c)} \le 0`$, "a child is funded only with its parent".
Both return `float` arrays. No Gurobi license is needed: the functions build arrays and never solve. About fifteen lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from matrices import needs_matrix, spend_matrix

# (id, start year, spend per year of the project)
projects = [("reservoir", 2050, [600.0, 200.0]), ("filter", 2051, [150.0]), ("tunnel", 2052, [90.0, 90.0])]
years = [2050, 2051, 2052]
print("spend matrix, years 2050-2052:")
print(spend_matrix(projects, years))
print("needs matrix, filter needs reservoir, tunnel needs filter:")
print(needs_matrix(projects, {"filter": "reservoir", "tunnel": "filter"}))

cases.says: projects that spend one year from the first year of the horizon put their cost in that row
each child gives one row with +1 in its column and -1 in its parent's
a project starting in a later year puts its k-th year of work in row start + k
spend falling after the last year of the horizon appears in no row
